To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the millipede diversity was higher in forest patches that are more isolated and that have less forested buffers.
soil millipede species richness and evenness were related to forest patch isolation, and to the amount of surrounding forest and presence of corridors in a matrix of urban development.
soil millipede species diversity is positively related with forest cover in the matrix and negatively related with the degree of patch isolation in urban landscapes of Puerto Rico.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how soil invertebrate biodiversity is related with landscape characteristics of tropical forests in Puerto Rico.
the relationship between soil millipedes and landscape structure.
the conservation of biodiversity in urbanizing tropical regions, where forest patches are increasingly surrounded by urban development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the millipede diversity of the 12 patches was related to the landscape structure surrounding them, rather than to patch attributes.
soil millipede species richness and composition in these tropical forest patches are related to their surrounding landscape structure and not to the patch attributes.
soil millipedes in forest patches of 30 years of age in Puerto Rico are influenced more by their surrounding landscape structure than by the attributes of the forest patches themselves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soil millipede communities in small forest patches of northeastern Puerto Rico are related to the amount of contiguous forest in the landscape, rather than patch attributes such as area and shape.

soil millipede species diversity was positively related to forested buffers and negatively with the degree to isolation of the patches, while the composition of millipede species was related to the presence of vegetation corridor and the distance to a reserve.

the diversity and composition of the soil millipede fauna in tropical forest patches is related to the degree of isolation, amount of forest within the matrix, and presence of corridors connecting to other forest patches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil invertebrates, and millipeds in particular, are sensitive to landscape fragmentation and that they can be used as indicators of landscape structure.

forest patches in urban areas are important for the conservation of soil biodiversity, and the presence of corridors and buffers of forested vegetation are key for the maintenance of soil invertebrate diversity.
the conservation and management plans of fragmented tropical habitats should include the spatial characteristics of the landscape and the surrounding matrix.
